summary: Four astronauts returned to Earth following an eight-month mission, marking a major milestone as NASA’s Crew-12 wrapped up its extended orbital stay. In civil spaceflight, NASA announced that plans for a lunar base are running ahead of schedule under a new space nuclear pact, while the agency solicits commercial space station proposals and demonstrates next-generation heat shield and in-space inspection technologies. Commercial and regulatory updates include proposed Department of Transportation changes to Part 450 commercial launch licensing rules, as venture funding flowed to defense space firms with Fortastra raising $30 million for security spacecraft and Kapta Space securing $24 million for radar payloads. For national security space, the U.S. Space Force completed personnel transfers from the Air Force under the Personnel Management Act, while European Earth observation providers announced plans to expand into satellite communications. Science highlights include NASA’s SPHEREx telescope detecting brown dwarfs with atmospheric water and methane, the first detection of variable exoplanet water clouds, and the pinpointing of the most distant fast radio burst ever detected. NASA also noted the death of Apollo software pioneer Margaret Hamilton at age 90. Looking ahead, readers should watch for an upcoming NASA media briefing highlighting the agency’s contributions to the Martian Moons Mission.
